answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 25 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the cedar solution is checked at the saffron gate and logged, the bridge audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore forfeits the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 14 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
